findings.title: website_name leaks TL0 website information to anonymous visitors
findings.body: `website_name` is added to the serializer attributes, but it is not added to `untrusted_attributes` alongside `website` (line 109). The old client derived the displayed name from `model.website`, which was hidden for anonymous visitors viewing TL0 profiles via `include_website?`. Now the server will emit `website_name` even when `website` itself is suppressed, exposing the website host and path to anonymous visitors for users whose website should be restricted. Add `:website_name` to the untrusted attributes list and ensure its include callback honors `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark
findings.body: The serializer conditional-include hook is defined as `def include_website_name` instead of `def include_website_name?`. ActiveModel serializers look for the `include_<attribute>?` form, so this method will not be called. As a result, `website_name` is always emitted as an attribute, including as `nil` for users without a website or with an invalid website URL, rather than being omitted when the condition is false. Rename the method to `def include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Naive label-count domain comparison treats unrelated subdomains as the same domain
findings.body: The `elsif` branch drops the first label and compares the remaining labels whenever both hostnames have more than two labels. This incorrectly treats two unrelated subdomains of a shared public suffix as the same domain. For example, if `Discourse.current_hostname` is `forum.blogspot.com` and the user's website is `http://random.blogspot.com/private`, `website_name` becomes `random.blogspot.com/private` even though the sites are not controlled by the same domain owner. Use a public-suffix-aware comparison or otherwise verify the registrable domain before deciding to append the URL path.
